themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 54 THIS WEEK, a 148% increase versus the 21.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.15), suggesting rapid pavement or infrastructure degradation across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 54 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 21.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.15, statistically significant)
1,020 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (750 alteration permits), suggesting active construction may be contributing to street damage
Repeated 'Other transportation infrastructure requests' in CB budget submissions indicate chronic unmet street maintenance needs
reporting_angles: Map the 54 complaints geographically: which blocks are worst affected and why?
Interview DOT about whether construction activity or seasonal thaw is driving the spike
Cross-check with DOB permits to see if major construction projects correlate with complaint clusters

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, signaling either a coordinated posting campaign or sudden enforcement gap.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average over 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35, highest severity anomaly in dataset)
Graffiti complaints also elevated at 10 last week vs. 3.8 average (167% spike), suggesting visual disorder accelerating
No corresponding news coverage or Reddit discussion detected, indicating story may be underreported locally
reporting_angles: Walk affected streets and photograph posting patterns—is this political, commercial, or event-driven?
Interview DSNY about whether staffing or enforcement changed this week
Check if illegal postings are concentrated near development sites (395 Flatbush, Columbia Heights rezoning) or transit hubs

themes_detail.label: Construction and Plumbing Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 26 THIS WEEK, up 139% from the 10.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.67), likely reflecting the 1,020 DOB permits filed in the past 90 days and indicating potential tenant and neighbor disruption.
evidence: 26 construction/plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly average (139% spike, z-score: 5.67)
1,020 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days, with 750 alteration permits dominating, indicating sustained building activity
Three active ULURP rezonings (395 Flatbush, Columbia Heights) in pipeline may drive future spike; 130 St. Felix permit already completed
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with active alteration permits about noise, dust, and access disruptions
Request DOB data on whether permits are concentrated geographically or tied to specific developers
Cross-reference complaint addresses with permit addresses to quantify overlap and tenant impact

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Concentrated in Commercial Zones
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged to 18 LAST WEEK, a 95% increase versus the 9.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.11), while street/sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 56 last week versus 17.8 average (216% spike, z-score: 4.24), indicating venue, traffic, or event-driven disruption.
evidence: Commercial noise: 18 complaints last week vs. 9.2 weekly average (95% spike, z-score: 5.11)
Street/sidewalk noise: 56 complaints last week vs. 17.8 weekly average (216% spike, z-score: 4.24), highest spike by rate in dataset
Residential noise remains steady at 1,812 over 90 days (non-spiking), suggesting outdoor/commercial noise is distinct issue
reporting_angles: Interview SLA about whether new bars, restaurants, or music venues recently opened or expanded in the district
Check if noise complaints cluster around specific intersections or entertainment corridors (Fulton Street, etc.)
Survey residents in high-complaint blocks about source (construction, traffic, events) and enforcement response time

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Infrastructure Failing
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints reached 19 LAST WEEK, a 145% increase from the 7.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.72), paired with elevated street condition complaints (54 this week), suggesting district-wide pavement and pedestrian infrastructure degradation.
evidence: Sidewalk condition complaints: 19 last week vs. 7.8 weekly average (145% spike, z-score: 4.72)
Street condition complaints: 54 THIS WEEK vs. 21.8 weekly average (148% spike), indicating paired infrastructure failure
CB budget submissions include repeated 'Other transportation infrastructure requests' to DOT, evidence of chronic, unresolved advocacy
reporting_angles: Walk main pedestrian corridors (Flatbush Ave, Fulton St, St. Felix) and document sidewalk hazards (cracks, buckling, tree damage)
Interview DOT about sidewalk repair backlog and timeline for addressing spiked complaints
Talk to elderly residents and parents about accessibility impact of deteriorating sidewalks
